Bahrain Overtime Calculator

Enter your salary and your overtime hours by day, at night, on the rest day and on holidays to see what the law says you are owed.

Prepared and reviewed by the Mustahaqati team · Last updated: 2026-11-03

Work out your overtime pay

The wage due to you; we assume total pay, as the law defines wage as everything you receive for your work.

Overtime rules in Bahrain

ItemRule
Normal hours8 a day unless agreed otherwise, and 48 a week (Article 51)
Ramadan6 a day or 36 a week for Muslim workers
Daily limit10 actual hours including overtime, within an 11-hour span (Article 53)
OvertimePay + 25% by day, + 50% at night between 7 pm and 7 am (Article 54)
Rest dayPay + 150% or a substitute day, at the worker's choice (Article 57)
Public holidaysAs for the rest day: + 150% or a substitute day (Article 64)
ExcludedThe employer's authorised agents, preparatory work, and guards and cleaners by decision (Article 56)

Example: A wage of BHD 6,000 with no allowances, so the hourly wage is 6,000 ÷ 30 ÷ 8 = BHD 25. Ten daytime hours: 10 × 25 × 1.25 = 312.500; four rest-day hours with the worker choosing pay: 4 × 25 × 2.5 = 250. Total BHD 562.500.

The law says "the wage due" without limiting it to basic pay, and defines wage as everything the worker receives for the work, so we assume total pay. End-of-service gratuity and pay in lieu of notice, by contrast, use basic pay plus the social allowance (Article 47).

To work out what you are owed when your contract ends, see the Bahrain end-of-service calculator and the notice period calculator. Prefer Arabic? Use the Arabic version.

Frequently asked questions

How is overtime calculated in Bahrain?

At the wage due plus 25% for daytime hours and 50% for night hours between 7 pm and 7 am (Article 54).

How much is rest-day work paid in Bahrain?

Pay plus 150%, or a substitute rest day, at the worker's choice (Article 57). No more than two consecutive rest days may be worked without written consent.

How much is public-holiday work paid in Bahrain?

As for the rest day: pay + 150% or a substitute day, at the worker's choice (Article 64).

What are the maximum working hours in Bahrain?

48 hours a week, with actual working time including overtime capped at 10 hours a day and an 11-hour span from start to finish.

Can I get time off instead of overtime pay in Bahrain?

No. Article 54 sets a cash rate for overtime; substitute days apply only to work on rest days and public holidays.

Sources

  • Bahrain Private Sector Labour Law 36/2012 — Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission: Articles 51 to 57 and 64 (Arabic)
  • Amendments register for Law 36/2012 — Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission
